films.title: Fast Action
films.description: Austin DePiano and Jon Schmoldt's 26-minute FA Skates full-length closes the book on the Illinois shop's 40-year run without treating the community as finished. Seven independently documented featured skaters anchor an end-title friends roll of 41 named appearances, turning three and a half years of filming into a broad Chicago and suburban-scene document.
creditNotes: Skate Jawn's authorized upload identifies Austin DePiano as editor, DePiano and Jon Schmoldt as principal filmers, and 12 additional camera contributors.

The exact film's end titles were visually reviewed in the controlled source player and preserve all 41 names explicitly billed as friends in order of appearance, plus Hunter Brown's photography and Lex Olander's title credit.

Skate Jawn's first-person DePiano interview and photo captions independently document featured appearances by Jon Schmoldt, Rex Smithburg, Tylor Horton, Sean McCaffrey, Steffen Watts, Zack Fisher and Zac Dugo. The article uses both Steffen and Steffan for Watts; the interview spelling is retained. No unsupported formal director credit is asserted.
films.locationNote: The first-person Skate Jawn feature establishes FA's Mount Prospect and broader Illinois roots and documents repeated Milwaukee filming trips; the record does not claim a complete spot-by-spot itinerary.
films.historicalContext: Filmed over three and a half years and completed after FA Skates closed in 2025, Fast Action is the final shop full-length in a 40-year local history and was conceived as an inclusive Illinois homie video rather than a conventional team release.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It shows a filmed wallride at a wooded DIY spot with dedicated red-and-black Fast Action title treatment and no trailer or episode labeling.

films.title: WHAT DID YOU EXPECT?
films.description: JP Blair's 33-minute East Coast full-length returns to a Jersey-heavy cast fourteen years after Outdated. Nine starring parts from Matt Andersen through Jake Baldini frame three deep montage sections, expanding the combined documented roster to 42 skaters across New York, New Jersey and the wider tri-state street scene.
creditNotes: JP Blair's filmmaker-channel upload supplies the nine starring riders and explicitly credits Blair with filming and editing.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the film as a 33-minute 2026 independent full-length and indexes 41 skaters. Combined with Josh Wilson, who is named in the filmmaker upload's nine-rider starring bill but omitted from that independent index, the defensible union is 42. Its soundtrack structure separates the principal parts from three montage sections and an outro.

SkateVideoSite indexes Jersey Dave, Matt Andersen, Jake Baldini and Juan Cuervo as production contributors without exposing defensible formal roles; they are retained as additional production credits rather than assigned invented titles.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: Skate Jawn identifies the project with New Jersey and New York, while Quartersnacks describes its Pennsylvania trio and tri-state filming context. SkateVideoSite documents New York spots; no complete spot-by-spot itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: WHAT DID YOU EXPECT? is JP Blair's first full-length since the 2012 video Outdated, reconnecting veteran East Coast figures and a current tri-state generation in one of 2026's most widely praised independent skate films.

films.title: PALACE DETROIT 313
films.description: Lev Tanju's 53-minute Palace Skateboards full-length captures seven years of the London brand returning to Detroit and becoming part of the city's skate and music culture. Fifteen documented riders bridge Palace's team with Detroit fixtures, filmed between August 2018 and November 2025 by head videographer Jack Brooks and five supported additional camera contributors.
creditNotes: Palace Skateboards' official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film. Vague explicitly bills it as a film by Lev Tanju, while contemporary Quartersnacks coverage documents Tanju's editing process and the project's cultural intent.

Bored of Southsea publishes the richest contemporary roster with all 15 featured riders and identifies Jack Brooks as head videographer plus Yoryo, Austin Bristow, Justin Bohl, Daniel Wheatley and Adam Todhunter as additional videographers.

NOTE, Office Hours and The Skateboarder's Companion independently corroborate the principal roster and seven-year Detroit production. Office Hours spells Shawn Powers as Shaun; the broader contemporary spelling Shawn is retained. No unsupported formal director credit is asserted.
films.locationNote: Multiple contemporary sources state that the complete film was shot entirely within Detroit city limits; no broader Michigan itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: Shot between August 2018 and November 2025, DETROIT 313 is Palace's seven-year Detroit document and the spiritual successor to 2017's London-set Palasonic, shaped as much by the city's music culture and long-term relationships as by the skating.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is a fisheye Detroit crew still specific to the complete film, with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.
